payload.recallText: Its the last unit of the year, I teach third grade. The last unit is the Oregon Trail. I am prepared to have my students live the Oregon trail. I usually teach topics like a game. We usually play the game and I am sort of a puppet master. I usually think of clever names as well such as caesar von salad, But the Oregon Trail is usually serious. So how do I teach this to 9 year olds who can even take the perspective of their younger sister. The Oregon trail was a journey that involved blizzards and hunger as people risk their whole lives to cross the Rockies of the now known America. Well I went to class and I say to my students, "were gonna learn about the Oregon Trail", One smart aleck kid named Alex says "Well will it be a game". I say "well yes but itll be a dangerous one". They get excited. I start pulling out the names and it the names of the real people who died on the oregon trail, we have chapman and now Alex is now Alex Bacon. Now we had to choose the occupations, and obviously all the girls said they wanted to be popstars. I told them lets stick to something more time appropriate so they were gold miners and merchants, and the occasional doctors.
